resources.string: Move text or small files between screens and cameras — no radio at all.

How it works
• The sender splits data into chunks and shows them as QR codes — two at a time (top: even chunks, bottom: odd chunks). Each code carries: transfer ID, index, total and the CRC-32 of the whole content (format QT1:ID:INDEX:TOTAL:CRC32:DATA).
• Data is packed with Base45 so the QR uses alphanumeric mode (≈30 % more data per code than base64). Text is compressed (DEFLATE) when that helps.
• The receiver reads both codes from one camera frame, in any order, shows which chunks are missing, and verifies the CRC-32 when complete.
• Acknowledgment tones: 1500 Hz = top code read, 2200 Hz = bottom code read, 2700 Hz (long) = all done. With "advance on tones" the sender listens with the microphone and advances each code independently as soon as its tone is heard (≈2× faster than one code); unconfirmed codes are resent after an adaptive timeout. Without it, the sender simply loops.
• PC → phone: open web/sender.html (single offline file) in a desktop browser; it can listen with the PC microphone too.

No internet, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or NFC is used. Keep the receiving phone ~20–40 cm from the screen so both codes are in view; lower the speed or chunk size if scanning is slow.

Optional, recommended. The receiver beeps 1500 Hz for the top code (even chunks) and 2200 Hz for the bottom code (odd chunks); the sender listens, advances each code as soon as its tone is heard, resends what was not confirmed, and stops on the 2700 Hz done tone. Without it, the codes simply loop.
